sections.name: File setup, mx, my, Point, clamp
sections.title: Map setup and coordinate conversion
sections.what: Sets the map size and includes helpers that turn longitude and latitude into positions on the drawn map, keep a point's data together, and stop panning from moving the map off the edge.
sections.why: Likely reason: the map is a flat drawing, so real coordinates must be converted to screen positions before anything can be drawn.
sections.watch_out: Latitude is limited to a fixed range, so points near the poles are drawn at the edge instead of their true spot.

sections.name: OpportunityGeography (part 1)
sections.title: Building map points and clusters
sections.what: Turns each signal location or linked project into a map point. Points are marked approximate when the location is only a country or sits close to a country centre. Nearby points are grouped into clusters that split apart as the user zooms in. Mouse and touch dragging is also handled here, so panning does not count as a click.
sections.why: Likely reason: clustering keeps crowded areas readable, and the approximate flag stops users reading a guess as a real site.
sections.watch_out: The 0.3 degree rule for spotting country-centre coordinates is a fixed guess. Changing it changes which markers look precise.

sections.name: OpportunityGeography (part 2)
sections.title: Zoom buttons, legend and cluster pop-up
sections.what: Adds zoom in, zoom out and reset buttons, a legend that explains circles, squares, solid and dashed markers, a credit for the map data, and a message when there are no points. When a cluster holds several items, a pop-up lists them and links to each signal or project.
sections.why: Likely reason: the legend and wording tell users how precise each marker is, so approximate points are not mistaken for sites.
sections.watch_out: The legend and empty-state wording are fixed text. If the meaning of a marker changes, these words must change too.

summary: Draws a zoomable, pannable world map of opportunity locations or linked Yard projects, and marks approximate locations so they are never read as exact sites.
purpose: Lets a user see where opportunities or linked projects are, while being clear about how precise each location is.
why: Likely reason: location data is often only a country or a country centre, so the map must show the uncertainty instead of presenting a guess as a real site.
how: Turns each location into a position on the map, marks it as approximate or recorded, groups nearby points into clusters that split apart as the user zooms in, draws the clusters over a world map image, and opens a single signal directly or a pop-up list for a cluster. Dragging pans the map, the mouse wheel zooms, and small drags are not counted as clicks.
inputs: A list of signals, a list of portfolio projects, the active region and country filters, which layer to show (opportunities or projects), and a callback for opening one signal.
outputs: An interactive map with clustered markers, zoom and reset buttons, a legend, a credit for the map data, and a pop-up list when a cluster holds several items. Calls the open callback when one signal is clicked.
risks: Approximate locations can be mistaken for real sites. The 0.3 degree rule for detecting country-centre coordinates is a fixed guess. Part of the point-building code is cut off in the packet, so its details are not checked here.
debug: If markers are missing, check the region and country filters and whether the location records have coordinates. If markers sit in the wrong place, check the latitude and longitude values and the projection. If panning or clicking feels wrong, check the drag threshold and the pointer handlers. If the background map does not load, check the map image path.
